#### expected date of next election
May 2025

## Government 23
### Judicial branch
**highest court(s):** Supreme Tribunal of Justice (consists of 32 judges organized into constitutional, political-administrative, electoral, civil appeals, criminal appeals, and social divisions)
**judge selection and term of office:** judges proposed by the Committee of Judicial Postulation (an independent body of organizations dealing with legal issues and of the organs of citizen power) and appointed by the National Assembly; judges serve nonrenewable 12-year terms
**subordinate courts:** Superior or Appeals Courts (Tribunales Superiores); District Tribunals (Tribunales de Distrito); Courts of First Instance (Tribunales de Primera Instancia); Parish Courts (Tribunales de Parroquia); Justices of the Peace (Justicia de Paz) Network

Venezuela Project or PV

## Government 23
### Diplomatic representation in the US
none
**note**: the embassy, which had been run by the Venezuelan political opposition, announced on 5 January 2023, that it had ended all embassy functions

## Government 23
### Diplomatic representation from the US
**chief of mission:** Ambassador (vacant); Chargé d’Affaires John McNAMARA (since 1 February 2025); note - serves as the chief of mission of the Venezuela Affairs Unit, located in the US Embassy, Bogota
**embassy:** Venezuela Affairs Unit, US Embassy, Carrera 45 N. 24B-27, Bogota, Colombia
**mailing address:** 3140 Caracas Place, Washington DC 20521-3140

### Independence
5 July 1811 (from Spain)

## Government 23
### National holiday
Independence Day, 5 July (1811)

The **Ecuadorian Civilian Space Agency** (**EXA**; Spanish: _Agencia Espacial Civil Ecuatoriana_) is a private Ecuadorian organization founded in 2007 that conducts research on space and planetary sciences. It is a non-profit non-governmental organization with civilian oversight.
EXA had tested microgravity via parabolic flight with the Ecuadorian Air Force. EXA launched Ecuador's first satellite, the CubeSatNEE-01 _Pegaso_, in April 2013 aboard a Chinese Long March 2D.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecuadorian_Civilian_Space_Agency#cite_note-wireduk20130426-2)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecuadorian_Civilian_Space_Agency#cite_note-sfn20130426-3) Its second satellite, the follow-on CubeSat NEE-02 _Krysaor_, was launched from Russia aboard a Dnepr rocket in November 2013.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecuadorian_Civilian_Space_Agency#cite_note-nasasf20131121-4)

1.   ↑The motto is meant to convey "From a dream to the stars," as the website says. However, the Latin is incorrect; the non-word _sominus_ has been substituted for the correct word _somnio._

EXA (Ecuadorian Space Agency) is a civilian, independent institution founded on November 1st, 2007 to lead the Ecuadorian Civilian Space Program, conduct planetary and space science research, and promote scientific development within the nation’s educational system. EXA is supported by the Ecuadorian State through a long-standing cooperation with the Ecuadorian Air Force.
With over 18 years of experience, EXA became the first institution in Ecuador to design, build, and place a satellite in orbit using fully indigenous technology. Since then, EXA has contributed hardware, engineering, and mission support to more than 148 satellites, 88 aerospace projects, and 8 complete missions worldwide.
EXA develops flight-proven subsystems for Small Satellites and Cube Satellites, including: power systems (solar cells, deployable arrays, EPS units, high-density batteries), mechanical and structural systems, onboard electronics, antennas, attitude-control solutions, and thermal-management components. Its technology has flown on multiple CubeSat, SmallSat, Space Tugs and even Launch Vehicle missions, consistently demonstrating reliability in extreme orbital environments.
EXA’s space hardware is commercially available through its official distributors: www.CubeSat.Market and www.SmallSat.Market, which provide global access to ITAR-free, space-qualified components for commercial, academic, and governmental operators.
EXA is also very active in cutting-edge space science and technology research trough the International Academy of Astronautics (IAA) and the American Institute for Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIAA)
By combining sovereign technological development with international collaboration, EXA delivers dependable and scalable solutions for the space industry.

EXA (Ecuadorian Space Agency) is a civilian, independent institution founded on November 1st, 2007 to lead the Ecuadorian Civilian Space Program, conduct planetary and space science research, and promote scientific development within the nation’s educational system. EXA is supported by the Ecuadorian State through a long-standing cooperation with the Ecuadorian Air Force.
With over 18 years of experience, EXA became the first institution in Ecuador to design, build, and place a satellite in orbit using fully indigenous technology. Since then, EXA has contributed hardware, engineering, and mission support to more than 148 satellites, 88 aerospace projects, and 8 complete missions worldwide.
EXA develops flight-proven subsystems for Small Satellites and Cube Satellites, including: power systems (solar cells, deployable arrays, EPS units, high-density batteries), mechanical and structural systems, onboard electronics, antennas, attitude-control solutions, and thermal-management components. Its technology has flown on multiple CubeSat, SmallSat, Space Tugs and even Launch Vehicle missions, consistently demonstrating reliability in extreme orbital environments.
EXA’s space hardware is commercially available through its official distributors: www.CubeSat.Market and www.SmallSat.Market, which provide global access to ITAR-free, space-qualified components for commercial, academic, and governmental operators.
EXA is also very active in cutting-edge space science and technology research trough the International Academy of Astronautics (IAA) and the American Institute for Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIAA)
By combining sovereign technological development with international collaboration, EXA delivers dependable and scalable solutions for the space industry.

The **Ecuadorian Civilian Space Agency** (**EXA**; Spanish: _Agencia Espacial Civil Ecuatoriana_) is a private Ecuadorian organization founded in 2007 that conducts research on space and planetary sciences. It is a non-profit non-governmental organization with civilian oversight.
EXA had tested microgravity via parabolic flight with the Ecuadorian Air Force. EXA launched Ecuador's first satellite, the CubeSatNEE-01 _Pegaso_, in April 2013 aboard a Chinese Long March 2D.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecuadorian_Civilian_Space_Agency#cite_note-wireduk20130426-2)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecuadorian_Civilian_Space_Agency#cite_note-sfn20130426-3) Its second satellite, the follow-on CubeSat NEE-02 _Krysaor_, was launched from Russia aboard a Dnepr rocket in November 2013.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecuadorian_Civilian_Space_Agency#cite_note-nasasf20131121-4)
